key_insight: MixTIME combines multiple pathology foundation models with a mixture-of-experts router to better predict immune biomarker expression from routine H&E slides.
clinical_relevance: By improving biomarker mapping and downstream tasks like survival prediction and report generation, this approach could support more precise oncology decision-making and tumor microenvironment analysis.
method: Integrates three expert modalities: image-only, image-text, and image-transcriptomic pathology foundation models.
Uses a learnable router to weight expert contributions at pixel and slide levels.
Trains with a distribution- and tendency-aware loss to predict multiplex immunofluorescence protein expression from H&E whole-slide images.
evidence_signal: The model was benchmarked on two datasets and reported state-of-the-art correlation performance across 17 protein markers, with added gains in spatial domain identification, survival prediction, and AI-assisted report generation.
watch_item: Performance is based on retrospective benchmark data, so real-world generalization, site-to-site robustness, and workflow integration still need prospective validation.
paper_title: Predicting Immune Biomarkers with MultiModal Mixture-of-Expert Pathology Foundation Models Empowers Precision Oncology
